title: A Metal That Does Not Corrupt
logline: A plain definition of metal is set down, then undone by the causes of corruption, the despair of the operators, and the price paid by those who chased an incorruptible root.

sources.title: Philosophiae chymicae IV vetustissima scripta : Tabula chymica
sources.author: Ibn-Umail, Muḥammad

citations.text: We say, therefore, that a metal is a fusible mineral body, extendable under the hammer in every dimension.
citations.attribution: Geber (Jabir ibn Hayyan / pseudo-Geber), Three Books on Alchemy, 1598 · p. 86

citations.text: The first is the triple cause of the corruption of each of the metals by fire.
citations.attribution: Geber (Jabir ibn Hayyan / pseudo-Geber), Three Books on Alchemy, 1598 · p. 195

citations.text: If, therefore, all causes of the corruption of metals agree, it is necessary that bodies be corrupted most of all.
citations.attribution: Ibn-Umail, Muḥammad, Philosophiae chymicae IV vetustissima scripta : Tabula chymica, 1605 · p. 272

citations.text: "Death is in the pot": which Nature hates.
citations.attribution: Gwinne, Matthew, Gold Not Gold, 1613 · p. 150

citations.text: For which reason, we too were brought into a stupor, and for a long space of time, we hid under the shade of despair.
citations.attribution: Geber (Jabir ibn Hayyan / pseudo-Geber), Three Books on Alchemy, 1598 · p. 222

citations.text: And Senior says: If blackness remains in it after its rubification, you have sinned in its preparation, and you have corrupted whatever you have worked, and you will die from the pain of sin and poverty, because these are incomparable riches.
citations.attribution: Ibn-Umail, Muḥammad, Philosophiae chymicae IV vetustissima scripta : Tabula chymica, 1605 · p. 199

citations.text: Is what is not granted to the instructed yielded to the unarmed?
citations.attribution: Gwinne, Matthew, Gold Not Gold, 1613 · p. 181

citations.text: To all these, our science does not reach.
citations.attribution: Geber (Jabir ibn Hayyan / pseudo-Geber), Three Books on Alchemy, 1598 · p. 29

citations.text: What if the form is incorruptible, inseparable, so that it remains gold?
citations.attribution: Gwinne, Matthew, Gold Not Gold, 1613 · p. 173

citations.text: For the Sun is the incorruptible root, and from the fire, and rust, and sulfurs, and therefore the true fixed tincture is extracted from it.
citations.attribution: Ibn-Umail, Muḥammad, Philosophiae chymicae IV vetustissima scripta : Tabula chymica, 1605 · p. 217

citations.text: What altar of faith, what anchor of hope?
citations.attribution: Gwinne, Matthew, Gold Not Gold, 1613 · p. 181
